title: RL 电路：电感电压的尖峰，电流的斜坡
summary: 方波驱动 100 Ω + 10 mH：电感两端是一跳一衰减的尖峰，电阻电压（= 电流 × R）是慢慢爬升的斜坡。
concepts: continuity of inductor current 电感电流不能突变
current via a resistor 用电阻电压看电流
description: 信号发生器（方波 ±1 V、1 kHz）→ R1（100 Ω）→ 结点 VL → L1（10 mH）→ GND。CH1 看输入，CH2 看 VL；电阻电压 = CH1 − CH2。

cards.title: 把电容换成电感
text: - 板上已经放好信号发生器和两个探头。加上 **R1 `100 Ω`**（**`b3`** → **`b10`**）和**电感 L1 `10 mH`**（**`c10`** → GND 轨）。电感就是绕成一圈圈的导线。
- 信号发生器：方波、**`1 kHz`**、幅度 **`1 V`**、偏置 **`0 V`**（在 −1 V 和 +1 V 之间跳）。CH1 看输入，CH2 看电感上端。
CH2 是什么样子？和 3.4 里电容上的电压比，像还是不像？

cards.title: 电感是一个沉重的飞轮
text: - 电容不让**电压**突变；电感不让**电流**突变。它像一个沉重的飞轮：转起来要时间，停下来也要时间。
- 方波一跳，电流来不及变，整个跳变只好全落在电感上：CH2 出现一个尖峰。之后电流慢慢跟上，电感上的电压也就消失了。
- 电感的电压和电流**变化的快慢**成正比。比如电流每毫秒变 1 mA：
$$v_L = L\frac{di}{dt} = 10 mH × \frac{1 mA}{1 ms}$$
![](fig:rl)
- 电流看不见，就看电阻：电阻电压 v_R = i × R，形状和电流一模一样。它在 CH1 和 CH2 之间。
![](fig:sch)

cards.title: 量电流的斜坡和电感的尖峰
text: - v_R 用两个通道相减：**CH1 − CH2**（示波器的 MATH 功能）。不要把接地夹夹到中间去。
- 读 v_R 的峰峰值和上升时间，再读 v_L 尖峰的最高值。
- 电流的时间常数是 τ = L / R总，R总 = 100 Ω + 50 Ω（信号发生器）+ 1 Ω（线圈）。
- 最后调到 **`10 kHz`**：半个周期比 τ 还短，v_R 变成什么样？

cards.title: 带走
text: - **电感电流不能突变**：v_L = L·di/dt。电流一变，电感就“顶”一个电压回去。
- **τ = L / R**：R 越大越快——和 RC 正好相反。
- **和 RC 对照**：电容电压连续、电流可以跳；电感电流连续、电压可以跳。
- **真实电路里**：突然切断电感电流，di/dt 极大，会冒出很高的反向电压，所以继电器线圈旁边要并一个续流二极管（5.4）。真实 10 mH 小电感的线圈电阻常有 10–30 Ω，比仿真的 1 Ω 大得多。

caption.text: v_L（电感）在每次跳变时冲到约 ±2 V 再衰减；v_R（电阻，形状和电流一样）在两次跳变之间按指数爬到新的值。

i18n.en: v_L (inductor) shoots to about ±2 V at every step and decays; v_R (resistor, the current's shape) climbs exponentially to its new value between steps.

caption.text: CH1 在 R1 左边，CH2 在电感上端：v_R = CH1 − CH2，v_L 就是 CH2。同一个电流 i 穿过两者。

i18n.en: CH1 left of R1, CH2 on top of the inductor: v_R = CH1 − CH2 and v_L is CH2. The same current i passes both.

en.title: RL circuit: spikes across the inductor, a ramp in the current
en.summary: A square wave drives 100 Ω + 10 mH: the inductor shows a spike that dies away, the resistor voltage (= current × R) a slowly climbing ramp.
en.description: Generator (square ±1 V, 1 kHz) → R1 (100 Ω) → node VL → L1 (10 mH) → GND. CH1 on the input, CH2 on VL; the resistor voltage = CH1 − CH2.
en.compare:
**Compare**: R_total = 100 + 50 + 1 = 151 Ω, τ = 10 mH / 151 Ω ≈ **66 µs** (rise time ≈ 2.2τ ≈ 146 µs).
- Steady current 1 V / 151 Ω ≈ 6.6 mA. Half a period, 0.5 ms, ≈ 7.5τ, so it settles every time: v_R between ±0.66 V, about **1.32 Vpp**.
- At each step nearly all of the 2 V lands on the inductor: v_L ideally ±1.99 V, read as about **1.9 V**, then decaying to a few millivolts across the coil resistance.
- **10 kHz**: half a period, 50 µs, < τ; v_R becomes nearly a triangle, Vpp ≈ 1.32 × tanh(0.38) ≈ **0.48 V**; the inductor voltage stays large because the current never stops changing.
hints: R1 from column 3 to column 10; L1 from column 10 to the GND rail.
v_R = CH1 − CH2; divided by 100 Ω it is the current.
τ = L / R_total, and R_total includes the generator's 50 Ω and the coil's 1 Ω.
tests: 1 kHz: v_L has positive and negative spikes at the steps; v_R settles in every half period
10 kHz (half a period < τ): the current can't finish, v_R shrinks

measurements.ask: 1 kHz: resistor voltage v_R (CH1 − CH2) peak-to-peak
measurements.explain: Steady current I = 1 V / 151 Ω ≈ 6.6 mA, so v_R swings ±0.66 V, about 1.32 Vpp.

measurements.ask: 1 kHz: the top of CH2's spike (inductor voltage v_L)
measurements.explain: At the step the current can't change, so nearly the whole 2 V step lands on the inductor: ideally 1 + 150/151 ≈ 1.99 V; sampling every 3.9 µs the scope reads about 1.9 V.

measurements.ask: 1 kHz: the rise time t_r of v_R (i.e. the current), 10 % to 90 %
From your t_r, the time constant τ = t_r / ln 9

measurements.explain: Half a period, 50 µs, < τ: the current only crawls back and forth in the middle: 1.32 V × tanh(T / 4τ) ≈ 0.48 V.

cards.title: Swap the capacitor for an inductor
text: - The generator and two probes are already on the board. Add **R1 `100 Ω`** (**`b3`** → **`b10`**) and an **inductor L1 `10 mH`** (**`c10`** → the GND rail). An inductor is just wire wound into a coil.
- Generator: square, **`1 kHz`**, amplitude **`1 V`**, offset **`0 V`** (jumping between −1 V and +1 V). CH1 on the input, CH2 on the top of the inductor.
What does CH2 look like? Is it like the capacitor voltage in 3.4, or not?

cards.title: An inductor is a heavy flywheel
text: - A capacitor won't let its **voltage** jump; an inductor won't let its **current** jump. It is like a heavy flywheel: it takes time to spin up and time to slow down.
- When the square wave steps, the current can't follow at once, so the whole step lands on the inductor: a spike on CH2. Then the current catches up and the inductor's voltage fades away.
- The inductor's voltage is proportional to **how fast its current changes**. For a current changing 1 mA per millisecond:
$$v_L = L\frac{di}{dt} = 10 mH × \frac{1 mA}{1 ms}$$
![](fig:rl)
- You can't see current, so watch the resistor: v_R = i × R has exactly the current's shape. It sits between CH1 and CH2.
![](fig:sch)

cards.title: Measure the current's ramp and the inductor's spike
text: - Get v_R by subtracting the channels: **CH1 − CH2** (the scope's MATH function). Don't move a ground clip to the middle.
- Read v_R's peak-to-peak and rise time, then the top of v_L's spike.
- The current's time constant is τ = L / R_total, with R_total = 100 Ω + 50 Ω (generator) + 1 Ω (coil).
- Finally set **`10 kHz`**: half a period is shorter than τ. What does v_R look like now?

cards.title: Take away
text: - **Inductor current can't jump**: v_L = L·di/dt. Change the current and the inductor pushes back with a voltage.
- **τ = L / R**: the larger R, the faster — the opposite of RC.
- **Next to RC**: a capacitor's voltage is continuous and its current may jump; an inductor's current is continuous and its voltage may jump.

- **In a real circuit**: break an inductor's current suddenly and di/dt is huge, so a high reverse voltage appears — that is why a relay coil gets a flyback diode (5.4). A real small 10 mH inductor often has 10–30 Ω of winding resistance, far more than the simulated 1 Ω.

tests.name: 1 kHz：v_L 在跳变处有正负尖峰；v_R 每半个周期都走到稳态
10 kHz（半个周期 < τ）：电流来不及走完，v_R 变小

compare:
**对比**：R总 = 100 + 50 + 1 = 151 Ω，τ = 10 mH / 151 Ω ≈ **66 µs**（上升时间 ≈ 2.2τ ≈ 146 µs）。
- 稳态电流 1 V / 151 Ω ≈ 6.6 mA。半个周期 0.5 ms ≈ 7.5τ，每次都走完：v_R 在 ±0.66 V 之间，约 **1.32 Vpp**。
- 跳变瞬间 2 V 几乎全落在电感上：v_L 理想值约 ±1.99 V，读到约 **1.9 V**，随后衰减到只剩线圈电阻上的几毫伏。
- **10 kHz**：半个周期 50 µs < τ，v_R 变成近似三角波，Vpp ≈ 1.32 × tanh(0.38) ≈ **0.48 V**；电感电压一直很大，因为电流一直在变。

measurements.ask: 1 kHz：电阻电压 v_R（CH1 − CH2）的峰峰值
measurements.explain: 稳态电流 I = 1 V / 151 Ω ≈ 6.6 mA，v_R 在 ±0.66 V 之间，约 1.32 Vpp。

measurements.ask: 1 kHz：CH2（电感电压 v_L）尖峰的最高值
measurements.explain: 跳变瞬间电流来不及变，2 V 的跳变几乎全落在电感上：理想值 1 + 150/151 ≈ 1.99 V；示波器每 3.9 µs 取一个点，读到约 1.9 V。

measurements.ask: 1 kHz：v_R（也就是电流）从 10% 升到 90% 的上升时间 t_r
由你的 t_r 算时间常数 τ = t_r / ln 9
调到 10 kHz：v_R 的峰峰值
measurements.explain: 半个周期 50 µs < τ，电流只在中间来回爬：1.32 V × tanh(T / 4τ) ≈ 0.48 V。

hints: R1 从第 3 列接到第 10 列；L1 从第 10 列接到 GND 轨。
v_R = CH1 − CH2；它除以 100 Ω 就是电流。
τ = L / R总，R总里要算上信号发生器的 50 Ω 和线圈的 1 Ω。
